subject: chemistry_2
question_text: Scandium is a transition element but zinc is not. Why?

mark_split.label: Scandium has a partly filled d subshell
Zinc is d¹⁰ in the atom and in the ion

verification.note: Unit 11 (d and f Block Elements) is sourced from the chemistry half of "FAST TRACK IPE for Sr. Students", printed chapter 8 ("8. d & f BLOCK ELEMENTS"), book pp.91-94, which prints this question on book p.91 as VSAQ 2. The 1+1 mark split is a CLAIM, not the board's, until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced, not invented. Neither the two-book union check nor a board back-test was possible for Chemistry-II: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is physics-only and first-year, and no second-year chemistry paper is in the corpus. BOOK CRITERION CORRECTED (book p.91, VSAQ 2): the printed answer tests for "unpaired d electron in the penultimate shell" — Sc is [Ar]3d¹4s² and has one, Zn is [Ar]3d¹⁰4s² and has none. That test gives the right answer for zinc by accident and the WRONG answer for copper: Cu is [Ar]3d¹⁰4s¹ and has no unpaired d electron either, yet Cu²⁺ is 3d⁹ and copper IS a transition element. The card uses the standard definition — a partly filled (incompletely filled) d subshell in the atom OR in one of its common ions — and states the copper case explicitly. TREND AND EXCEPTIONS NAMED HERE: Zn, Cd and Hg are the d-block metals excluded by the strict definition; Cr ([Ar]3d⁵4s¹) and Cu ([Ar]3d¹⁰4s¹) are the two first-series configurations that do not follow the plain 3d^x 4s² pattern.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question
d and f Block Elements — 2 marks

steps.label: Scandium is a transition element
lines: A transition element has a partly filled
d subshell in the atom or in one of its
The 3d subshell holds one electron out of
ten, so it is partly filled.
steps.why: The definition is about a partly filled d subshell, not about which block an element is placed in. Scandium has 3d¹ in the free atom, which is partly filled, so it passes the test on the atom alone. Its only common ion, Sc³⁺, is 3d⁰ — which is why Sc³⁺ is colourless and diamagnetic even though scandium itself is a transition element.
common_mistakes: Saying every d-block element is a transition element. Zn, Cd and Hg lie in the d block but do not meet the definition.
Testing the ion only. Sc³⁺ is 3d⁰, but the atom Sc is 3d¹, and the atom is enough.
steps.memory_tip: Test the atom first, then the common ions. One partly filled d subshell anywhere is enough.
steps.margin_note: Write the configuration [Ar] 3d¹ 4s² and the words "partly filled". The definition on its own is half this mark.

steps.label: Zinc is not
lines: a completely filled subshell, so zinc
fails the test in both forms.
Zn, Cd and Hg are d-block metals but
Copper passes on its ion instead: Cu is
steps.why: Zinc fails the test twice over — the atom is 3d¹⁰ and its only common ion, Zn²⁺, is also 3d¹⁰ — so no partly filled d subshell exists in either. Cadmium and mercury fail in the same way. Copper is the opposite case and is the reason the ions must be tested: the atom has no partly filled d subshell, but Cu²⁺ is 3d⁹, so copper is a transition element. Two first-series configurations are also not the plain 3d^x 4s² pattern at all — Cr is [Ar] 3d⁵ 4s¹ and Cu is [Ar] 3d¹⁰ 4s¹ — because the half-filled and completely filled d sets are lower in energy.
common_mistakes: Writing Zn²⁺ as 3d⁸. The 4s electrons are removed first, so Zn²⁺ is 3d¹⁰ 4s⁰.
Ruling copper out on the atom alone. Cu is 3d¹⁰ 4s¹, but Cu²⁺ is 3d⁹, so copper is a transition element.
steps.memory_tip: Zn, Cd and Hg are the three d-block metals that are not transition metals: d¹⁰ in the atom and d¹⁰ in the ion.
steps.margin_note: Both configurations, atom and ion, are needed. Naming Cd and Hg beside zinc costs one line and shows the rule.

insider_note: The examiner is looking for the phrase "partly filled d subshell", applied to the atom AND to its common ions. Configurations written without that phrase are usually worth half.
